verses.text: The LORD's message came to me:
"Son of man, speak to your people and tell them: 'Suppose I bring a sword against a land, and the people of that land choose one of their men to be their watchman.
When he sees the sword coming against the land, he blows the trumpet to warn the people.
Then if anyone hears the trumpet but does not pay attention to the warning, and the sword comes and kills them, they are responsible for their own death.
They heard the trumpet but did not pay attention to the warning, so they are responsible for their own death. If they had paid attention, they would have saved their life.

But if the watchman sees the sword coming and does not blow the trumpet to warn the people, and the sword comes and kills someone, that person will die because of their own sin. But I will hold the watchman responsible for their death.'
Son of man, I have made you a watchman for the people of Israel. Whenever you hear a message from my mouth, warn them for me.

When I say to the wicked, 'Wicked person, you will surely die,' and you do not speak out to warn them to turn from their ways, that wicked person will die for their sin. But I will hold you responsible for their death.
But if you warn the wicked person to turn from their ways and they do not turn, they will die for their sin, but you will have saved yourself.
Son of man, say to the people of Israel, 'You are saying, "Our wrongs and our sins weigh us down, and we are wasting away because of them. How can we live?"'

Tell them, 'As surely as I live, says the Lord GOD, I take no pleasure in the death of the wicked. I want them to turn from their ways and live. Turn back! Turn back from your evil ways! Why should you die, people of Israel?'

Son of man, say to your people, 'If righteous people sin, their past righteousness will not save them. And if wicked people turn from their wickedness, their past wickedness will not bring them down. Righteous people who sin will not be allowed to live because of their past righteousness.

If I tell righteous people that they will surely live, but then they trust in their righteousness and do evil, none of the right things they did will be remembered. They will die for the evil they have done.
And if I say to wicked people, "You will surely die," but then they turn from their sin and do what is fair and right,
if they return what they took as security for a loan, give back what they stole, follow the rules that give life, and do no evil, they will surely live. They will not die.
None of the sins they committed will be held against them. They have done what is fair and right, and they will surely live.
Yet your people say, "The Lord's way is not fair." But it is their way that is not fair.
If righteous people turn from doing right and do evil, they will die for it.
And if wicked people turn from their wickedness and do what is fair and right, they will live because of it.
Yet you say, "The Lord's way is not fair." People of Israel, I will judge each of you by your own ways.'"
On the fifth day of the tenth month, in the twelfth year of our exile, a man who had escaped from Jerusalem came to me and said, "The city has fallen!"
The evening before the man arrived, the LORD's power had come on me. He opened my mouth before the man came to me in the morning. So my mouth was opened, and I was no longer silent.
Then the LORD's message came to me:

"Son of man, the people living in the ruins in the land of Israel are saying, 'Abraham was only one man, and yet he took over the land. But we are many. Surely the land has been given to us as our own.'
So tell them, 'This is what the Lord GOD says: You eat meat with the blood still in it, look to your idols for help, and spill blood. Should you then take over the land?
You rely on your swords, you do disgusting things, and each of you commits adultery with your neighbor's wife. Should you then take over the land?'

Tell them, 'This is what the Lord GOD says: As surely as I live, those living in the ruins will die by the sword. Those out in the country I will give to wild animals to be eaten. Those in fortresses and caves will die of disease.
I will make the land a desolate wasteland, and its proud strength will come to an end. The mountains of Israel will be so desolate that no one will travel through them.
Then they will know that I am the LORD, when I have made the land a desolate wasteland because of all the disgusting things they have done.'
As for you, son of man, your people are talking about you by the walls and at the doors of their houses. They say to each other, 'Come and hear the message that has come from the LORD.'

My people come to you, as they usually do, and sit in front of you. They listen to your words, but they do not put them into practice. With their mouths they say how much they love me, but their hearts are greedy for unjust gain.
To them you are nothing more than someone who sings love songs with a beautiful voice and plays an instrument well. They hear your words, but they do not put them into practice.
When all this comes true, and it surely will, then they will know that a prophet has been among them."
